solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lofty approach of Charlie, trendy still?

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet
hip means fashionable
a still is a single photograph, a shot

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Charlie's high-flown style is still in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like an adverb but is a noun here, a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a chip shot is a short lofted stroke played to approach the green.

clue.text: Dull account recalled type of knitwear craft

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters go back in reverse

parts.note: mat or matt means not shiny
AC is the abbreviation for account
Aran is a style of chunky cabled knitting

explanation.surface: A boring report recalled a type of woolly handicraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like a handicraft beside knitwear, but it means a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a boat with two parallel hulls, a sailing vessel.

clue.text: Turning over note to obtain National Insurance number

indicators.note: turning over flips the sequence, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: re is a note of the sol-fa scale
to obtain is to get
NI is the abbreviation for National Insurance, the UK social security contribution

explanation.surface: Flipping a document over to find one's National Insurance number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National Insurance number' is a real UK identifier, so the definition hides inside a familiar phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a whole number, with no fractional part.

clue.text: Group travelling by sea or coach

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large shoal of fish swimming together
second meaning: to train or teach

explanation.walkthrough: The surface offers two ways to travel, boat or coach, but coach is a verb meaning to instruct.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish swim in shoals, and to educate or train someone is another sense of the same word.

clue.text: One visits troubled region at issue

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so this letter is placed within the others
troubled means disturbed, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A person goes to a strife-torn area that is in dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at issue' reads as a phrase, but issue alone is the verb definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to arise or spring from a source, as to issue does.

clue.text: Root and branch from wide shrub

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide
holly is an evergreen shrub

explanation.surface: Roots and branches taken from a broad bush, as a gardener might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Root and branch' is an idiom for completely, though the surface makes it parts of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom root and branch means thoroughly and entirely, an adverbial equivalent of completely.

clue.text: Comfortable with hitmen's promise?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: killers vowing that they will kill, off being slang for murder

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second reading, splitting the answer into we'll and off.
explanation.definitionFit: Being comfortable can mean having enough money to live well, which is being wealthy.

clue.text: Slip fielder makes public disagreement about finale to match

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the pair of words goes around a letter

parts.note: overt means open, public

indicators.note: the finale is the end, so only the last letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the last letter of the word
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A slip catcher in cricket falls out loudly with someone over the end of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an overthrow is a fielder's wild return that the keeper misses, giving away extra runs; 'Slip' is a slip-up, not the fielding position.
explanation.definitionFit: An overthrow is a fielding mistake, the sort of slip a fielder makes when returning the ball.

clue.text: Rising star getting ovation, outwardly showing restraint

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: Rigel is a bright star in Orion

indicators.note: outwardly means only the outside, so just the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming celebrity is applauded but still looks held back.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg-iron is a shackle fastened round the ankle to restrain a prisoner.

clue.text: Mild reprimand: who'd be a mummy!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the clicking sound of mild disapproval
second meaning: the familiar short name of the pharaoh Tutankhamun, now a mummy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Who'd be a mummy!' reads as an exasperated parent's sigh, but it points to the famous mummified Egyptian king.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection expresses disapproval, and the same letters are the nickname of the boy pharaoh whose embalmed body was found in 1922.

clue.text: Travelling around led here: big German town

indicators.note: things travelling around move from place to place, so the following letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: the three words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A traveller explains that wandering brought them to a large German town.
explanation.definitionFit: Heidelberg is a university town on the Neckar in south-west Germany.

clue.text: Some sail on gamely after reversing bloomer

indicators.note: reversing means the run of letters is read from right to left
only some of the letters of the words that follow are used, a run inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Keep sailing bravely after turning the boat round, a skipper's advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' sounds like a blunder, but here it is a plant that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnolia is a tree or shrub prized for its large showy flowers, so it is a flowering plant.

clue.text: Protest defeat in shouting match?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a loud public objection
second meaning: to cry louder than a rival, beating them at shouting

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the word as out plus cry, as one says outrun or outshine.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a vehement public complaint, and as a verb it means to cry more loudly than another.

clue.text: Painter with colour running short getting little done

indicators.note: running short means it lacks its final part, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter
red is a colour

explanation.surface: An artist short of paint gets hardly any work finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little done' sounds like idleness but describes meat cooked lightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare steak is cooked only briefly, so it is barely done in the kitchen sense.

clue.text: I agree just to follow English military command

indicators.note: to follow means come after, so these parts are placed behind the next one

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
yes expresses agreement
just means fair, right

explanation.surface: Someone simply concedes that they will go along with the English.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes right is the parade-ground order for troops to turn their heads to the right in salute.

clue.text: Second dismissal having unfortunate consequences

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it
a firing is a dismissal from a job

explanation.surface: Sacking someone a second time turns out badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan that is backfiring produces the opposite of its intended effect, harming its maker.

clue.text: Furry creature put out with a dog requiring attention

parts.note: KO is a knockout, putting someone out
taken as written
a lab is a Labrador dog
to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A furry animal annoyed by a dog that wants looking after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' looks like annoyed, but it is a knockout.
explanation.definitionFit: The koala is a tree-dwelling Australian marsupial with thick grey fur.

clue.text: Voting for August the ninth to hold race

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so the voting letters go within

parts.note: august means grand, majestic
IX is nine in Roman numerals
PR is proportional representation, a voting system

explanation.surface: An election is set for the ninth of August, with a race to be held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'August' looks like the month, but is the adjective meaning grand.
explanation.definitionFit: A Grand Prix is a major international motor race in the Formula One championship.

clue.text: Schedule when match or rearranged heat may end

indicators.note: something rearranged has had its parts put in a different order

parts.note: the three words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A sports organiser fixes when a game or a rescheduled qualifying race should finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks sporting, as does heat, but here it means a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: To name the day is to fix the date of one's wedding, a match being a marriage.

clue.text: One turned to horse by a dramatist, she to something smaller

indicators.note: turned to means changed into, so one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: taken as written
Jean Racine was a French tragedian
I is the Roman numeral one, the letter to be replaced
H is slang for heroin, horse

explanation.surface: A tale of metamorphosis: one person becomes a horse in a play, another something tiny.
explanation.walkthrough: In RACINE the I is changed to H. In Greek myth Athena turned the weaver Arachne into a spider.
explanation.definitionFit: Arachne was the mortal weaver whom Athena transformed into a spider, a much smaller creature.

clue.text: Discover Sky broadcasting

parts.note: to sky a ball is to hit it up high
a programme being broadcast is on air

explanation.surface: Finding out about the Sky television network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sky' looks like the satellite broadcaster, but it is a verb from cricket and golf.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit upon something is to find or think of it by chance.

clue.text: Health agency auxiliaries initially hold it

parts.note: the World Health Organization

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A health body's support staff are told to wait first.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoa is the command to stop, the same as saying wait or stay put.

clue.text: Bob, perhaps, and Ruth involved with CIA

indicators.note: involved means entangled, so the letters are mixed together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bob and Ruth are mixed up with American spies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name beside Ruth, but it is a hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a short hairstyle cut level around the head, one example of a trim.

clue.text: Deck idiot descending on ambassador

indicators.note: in a down clue descending on means coming above, so this part goes first

parts.note: a clot is a fool
HE is His Excellency, an ambassador's title

explanation.surface: Punch the fool who swoops down on a diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' looks like punch to the floor, but it means dress.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck someone out is to dress or adorn them in clothes.

clue.text: Go off in pursuit of normal copy

indicators.note: in pursuit of means coming behind, so this part follows the other

parts.note: par is the normal or standard level
food that goes off rots

explanation.surface: Someone chases after an ordinary duplicate.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat or imitate mechanically, as the talking bird mimics speech.

clue.text: Resident often on the wing (spell initiated by judge)?

definitions.text: Resident often on the wing (spell initiated by judge)?

parts.note: surface reading: a creature that spends its time flying
setter's reading: an inmate of a prison wing, serving a sentence that a judge imposed

explanation.walkthrough: A wing is a section of a prison, and a spell is a term inside; bird is also slang for a prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual prisoner who lives on a cell block is a convict, nicknamed after a caged bird.

clue.text: 3 peers with time to see cult leader

parts.note: 3 is the answer to 3-down, and a high school is a kind of it
peers means looks closely, prying
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Pupils, nobles and time are gathered to visit a sect's head.
explanation.walkthrough: The 3 points to 3-down; HIGH is a type of that, as in high school. 'peers' looks like nobles, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A high priest is the chief religious figure of a cult or temple.

clue.text: Take complaint from mostly despicable character

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to cure is to take away an ailment

explanation.surface: Accepting grievances from a largely contemptible person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' looks like a grievance but means an illness, which a remedy takes away.
explanation.definitionFit: A cur is a mongrel dog, and figuratively a contemptible man.

clue.text: Church worker's relations from the south?

parts.note: sexual relations
coming from the south means heading to the north, TO N

explanation.surface: A verger's relatives who come from the south of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relations' looks like family, but here it means intercourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton is a church officer who looks after the building and graveyard.

clue.text: What might be extra eg if nitrogen's involved?

definitions.text: What might be extra eg if nitrogen's involved?

indicators.note: involved means twisted together, so the letters are tangled into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: An additional charge might be levied when nitrogen emissions are concerned.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a levy on emissions such as nitrogen oxides is an extra cost.
explanation.definitionFit: A green tax is an environmental levy, an extra charge imposed on polluting activities.
